brief.goal: Understand how solar panels convert sunlight into electricity and how batteries store that energy for later use.
keyPoints: Solar panels (photovoltaic cells) capture sunlight and convert it directly into electricity.
Batteries act as storage units, holding the generated electricity to be used when the sun isn't shining.
constraints: Beat 1 Title: Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity; Beat 1 Audience text: Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity.
Beat 2 Title: Batteries store electricity for later use; Beat 2 Audience text: Batteries store electricity for later use.
No extra claims beyond the key points.
Do not guarantee continuous power supply.

flow.title: Solar Energy Introduction
flow.summary: This three-minute presentation introduces solar energy for teachers, explaining how solar panels convert sunlight into electricity and how batteries store that energy for later use. The flow uses a simple conceptual diagram to illustrate the process without making claims about cost, efficiency, or continuous power supply.

beats.title: Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity
beats.audienceText: Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity.
beats.speakerNotes: Explain that solar panels, made of photovoltaic cells, capture sunlight and convert it directly into usable electricity. This is the first step in the solar energy process.
beats.visualDirection: Show the conceptual diagram illustrating how sunlight enters the solar panel and becomes electricity.

beats.speakerNotes: Explain that batteries act as storage units, holding the generated electricity to be used when the sun isn't shining. This allows energy to be available at night or during cloudy days.
beats.visualDirection: Show the diagram highlighting how electricity is stored in the battery and then released as stored electricity.
